courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Students will learn the basics of front-end web development, code management, and the tools of web development including version control using Git and GitHub . Course topics and activities include a review of the web in general, how it works from the internet layer to the application layer, and how to create basic multi-page web sites. Students will register a domain name, secure their own web space and learn to operate basic web services including File transfer (FTP) and admin features. S udents will also review the latest versions of HTML and CSS. Learning will focus on web standards as outlined by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) to cod e HTM L and CSS to control hierarchy structure, functionality, layout and appearance of websites while creating modern, standards compliant, semantic and accessible markup for a web site. The coding process from design to publishing a web site to the public internet will be covered. Evaluation will include lab assignments and projects. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course covers the theory and best practices of web design fundamentals. Topics include screen-design principles; web layout and design; digital colour theory; typography fundamentals; image and web graphics sourcing, handling and copyright. Students will learn the best practices in creating designs for responsive web sites that adapt to different screen sizes using the fundamental design and usability principles for layout, such as visual hierarchy, colours, fonts, readability, proportions, alignments, and white space. In this class, students will explore in detail the differences between raster and vector graphics and basic techniques suitable for digital image creation, manipulation, and management. Students will develop practical skills will be developed in how to colour correct, resize, and resample images as well as how to use transparency settings and automate the resizing and saving of large numbers of images for the web. Evaluation will include lab assignments. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: User Experience (UX) plays a critical role in the success of products and services. This course will focus on the theory of website UX planning, the design process, and the integration of UX into the web design and development process. Students will learn the fundamentals of defining requirements, creating information architecture, and evaluating solutions using usability testing techniques. This course will use a combination of lectures, in-class discussions, hands-on exercises, group work, and tool demonstrations. Evaluation will include a combination of group and individual assignments. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Modern web sites and applications demand dynamically and constantly updated content and interactive user interfaces. This course introduces the JavaScript programming language as well as foundational programming concepts to provide the services and features that industry demands. Students will be introduced to general computer programming concepts such as variables, conditional statements, loops, functions, objects and classes. By applying these basic programming concepts students will explore the development of interactive web experiences such as slide shows, animated navigation systems, tabs, accordions, lightboxes and other common web widgets. Manipulating and traversing an HTML document with JavaScript using the browser's DOM API will also be discussed.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course covers how to use Generative AI (GenAI) tools to enhance learning and increase productivity while working on web development and design projects. The three-day course will be spread across multiple months to integrate with more advanced topics learned later in the FWD program. The first class will focus on what GenAI is and how to use GenAI tools for learning. In the second class, students will learn how to use GenAI tools for code review and how to use agentic GenAI for code creation. In the final class, students will form small teams and attempt to build a new, complex web project entirely with GenAI to assess the feasibility of the process and the quality of the result. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: (65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200)
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course focuses on collaborative front-end web development practices used in modern team environments. Building on prior studies, students will learn how to integrate user-centered thinking, design systems, and front-end web development techniques into a collaborative workflow using industry-standard tools. Students will practice how to collaboratively manage code using version control systems such as GitHub, including branching, merging, pull requests, and code reviews. Students will work with collaborative UX design tools to create, interpret, and implement information architecture, design systems, components, and high-fidelity mock-ups, translating design specifications into functional and accessible user interfaces. Students will be introduced to project management tools to support task organization, team coordination, and workflow planning in a collaborative setting, working through an end-to-end design-to-development process. Prerequisite(s): (65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200)

This course is an overview of common project management concepts which will be applied to the collaborative projects in the later courses. The course includes the basic concepts of web project management, teamwork, and an introduction to popular project management software applications used in the web development field. Students will apply their knowledge and skills as well as appropriate tools and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements in later courses. Students will engage in project planning, identify project stakeholders, define the roles and responsibilities of the team, define project scope, devise risk and quality plans, map out schedules, and learn about time tracking and documentation. Evaluation will include in-class assignments. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000

This course shifts the focus from client-side to server-side programming utilizing PHP and MySQL. An introduction to PHP fundamentals and the role it plays in generating dynamic websites will be covered. Students will explore the differences between client-side and server-side scripting, learning to identify when scripting solutions are appropriate. They will apply basic scripting techniques, write and use functions, validate HTML forms, utilize regular expressions, and implement cookie management and session handling. Additionally, students will learn to design and implement relational databases using MySQL, write basic SQL queries for data manipulation, and use PHP to interact with and manage databases. Evaluation will include assignments and a project. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000

The Web Scripting 3 course introduces students to JavaScript-based web application development. The course explores setting up and developing a web application using modern JavaScript build systems. Students will learn how to implement modern coding methodologies available in JavaScript such as modules and classes. Application state management will be explored in detail along with routing, validating user data and styling modules. Utilizing foundational JavaScript skills and modern JavaScript coding and build system techniques, students will explore developing and deploying full-featured web applications. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 1000 and FWDP 1400

This course covers the fundamental features of dynamic websites and the creation of custom-coded websites built with a Content Management System (CMS). Students will learn the basics of dynamic websites, how they are used to create a CMS, and how to work with a CMS to build websites. Students will create, configure, and migrate websites built using a CMS. Once they understand the basic features, students will create custom code to extend functionality, edit and create templates, and build a basic web app or website on a CMS. To prepare them for their Capstone Project, students will also create a development plan for a mock client website. Evaluation will include lab assignments and projects. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 2400

This course focuses on the multiple platforms and solutions that can be used to create and launch an online store. These include open source and Software as a Service (SaaS) platforms to provide a foundation for work with e-commerce solutions Course topics include all stages of the preparation, configuration, and setup of a secure online store. Students will determine the appropriate tools necessary to configure and securely operate an online store for various products and services. Learners will then review tool features, configure settings for product samples, price options, and manage shipping options. Students will also learn and use the relevant templating or theming languages and methods to customize the design, layout, and functionality of their online store and further customize functionality using extensions. Once the store is set up, students will use best practices to secure the store, connect payment gateways, and test the payment process to complete the entire e-commerce purchasing process. Evaluation will include assignments. Prerequisite(s): FWDP 3600

courses.prerequisite_raw: 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200
courses.course_overview_raw: The focus of this course is to plan a front-end web development-related career, and at the same time, prepare to showcase a body of digital work created in and outside the program. This includes personal and professional development designed to support career success. Students will research trends, employment, and entrepreneurship to create a career plan. They will also create a fully functional, publicly accessible, professional-level portfolio website based on after-program career goals and industry expectations. At the end of the course project, students will have a portfolio website that demonstrates their skills using HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, JavaScript frameworks, and optionally server-side programming and/or content management systems. Students will also develop their personal brand, create a competitive resume and cover letter and learn advanced interview skills. Evaluation will include the project and workshop participation. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 1000 and 65% in FWDP 1100 and 65% in FWDP 1200

courses.prerequisite_raw: 65% in FWDP 2100 and 65% in FWDP 2300 and 65% in FWDP 3700
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course is the culmination of the knowledge and learning in the Front-End Web Development program and the practical application and development of skills gained in earlier courses. This course will introduce students to the professional practice of working on a small web development team to build a mid-sized custom dynamic website. Throughout the supervised project, students will use industry best practices to develop a website based on specific business and functional requirements. To manage their tasks and meet deadlines, students will work collaboratively using communication and management tools common in the industry. All teams will have scheduled meetings with the instructor to track their progress and will present tutorials to the class on topics they research during their projects. Evaluation will be based on the project. Evaluation will be based on the project. Prerequisite(s): 65% in FWDP 2100 and 65% in FWDP 2300 and 65% in FWDP 3700

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes April and September each year. Please see the program overview for precise dates. Application processing Applications are accepted during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) April September 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* September January 1st* Domestic students: September 21st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. Applications are considered for a specific intake. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet the following entrance requirement and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains: English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. ( CIPC : 11.0801) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies
